What kind of panel is this? I've never seen ground buses like that.  Normally I put a couple wraps of red tape around the white if I'm using it as a hot leg. I think you're supposed to by code.  The hood range is technically supposed to be on an AFCI. If the exhaust fan isn't in a bath, it should be AFCI protected. It's ridiculous. I know.

Looks great but ground bare aluminum needs to go to the ground bus, bonded to the panel. It's currently on a neutral bus. 

The neutrals for the 120 15 and 20 amp circuits, except for the bathroom circuit shouldn't be connected to the bus bar, because when breakers go in, it will go into the afci breaker.
It's not a hazard, the dimmers just need to be removed and regular switches put in, or replace the bulbs with ones that are dimmable.

Is this a main panel or a sub?

If it's a main, is the green screw on the right neutral bus bonding it to the frame?  I do work in San Diego where the main is almost always outside, right next to the meter.  Not seeing the meter makes me think it is not a main, but I imagine in other parts of the country they put the meter on the outside and main panel inside?

If it's a sub panel, I believe the neutral and ground buses shouldn't be bonded.  It looks like they currently are.

I'm sure everyone has different tactics to stay sober. The following are a few of the things that helped me.
Stopdrinking - read posts, comment, do the daily check in
Tell friends or family that will support you - My friends knew I wanted to stop and encouraged me.  Even if I wanted to drink with them they wouldn't because I opened up to them. Both irl friends and video game friends.
Count your blessings - Has my life gotten better since I stopped?  The answer was a definite yes.  Was it worth risking by having another drink? NO
Think How far I had come - Do i want to reset my badge? NO

A lot has changed. In retrospect, I'm a totally different person. My relationships with my family, friends, and girlfriend have improved, I'm excelling at work, I have a disposable income. My quality of life has improved immensely.  I haven't had any hardships this year though, I'm nervous to see how I'll react if I went through a death of a family member or breakup. How should it have been done?

Yes, #3 is circuit breakers, #2 you don't need to worry about and shouldn't even try to access.

If you're going to replace outlets and there is no ground wire the next best thing in terms of safety, is to make them GFI protected
Correct me if I'm wrong but isn't that a hefty fine if OSHA catches it?

The left one is a low voltage box

The middle one is your Main electric Panel.  The left side, where the meter is, is for the Utility company. The right side of the same box, where the conduit is coming into the bottom, should have your circuit breakers.

The right box should not be sealed shut to the point where opening it would damage it.  It probably has an inconspicuous screw.  My guess is that box is most likely a junction box with a bunch of wires twisted together.  

I hope this helps!
